ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Given the diagram, $P$ is a point inside the right-angled triangle $ABC$ where $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, and $PA=3$, $PB=7$, $PC=9$. What is the maximum value of $BC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw PD$\perp$AB at D, PF$\perp$AC at F, then draw BG$\perp$PF at G through B, and CE$\perp$PD at E through C, intersecting BG at H, connect AH, PH\\
$\because$ $\angle$BAC$=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ the quadrilaterals ADPF, ADEC, ABGF, PGHE, and ABHC are all rectangles\\
$\therefore$ PD=BG, PF=AD=EC, PG=HE, BC=AH\\
$\therefore$ $PA^{2}=AD^{2}+PD^{2}=PF^{2}+PD^{2}$\\
$PC^{2}=EC^{2}+PE^{2}=PF^{2}+PE^{2}$\\
$PH^{2}=PE^{2}+HE^{2}=PE^{2}+PG^{2}$\\
$PB^{2}=PG^{2}+BG^{2}=PG^{2}+PD^{2}$\\
$\therefore$ $PB^{2}+PC^{2}=PA^{2}+PH^{2}=PF^{2}+PE^{2}+PG^{2}+PD^{2}$\\
$\because$PA=3, PB=7, PC=9\\
$\therefore$ $7^{2}+9^{2}=3^{2}+PH^{2}$,\\
Solving gives $PH=11$\\
$\because$ in $\triangle PAH$, PA=3, $PH=11$\\
$\therefore$ $8<AH<14$\\
$\because$ when points A, P, H are collinear, $AH=14$\\
$\therefore$ when points A, P, H are collinear, $BC=AH=14$ is the maximum\\
Hence, the answer is: $BC=\boxed{14}$.

method.method_draft: Use a coordinate/rectangle completion route. First read the diagram as a right triangle with A as the right-angle vertex, B and C forming the opposite side BC, and interior point P joined to A, B, C. From the text take angle BAC = 90° and PA=3, PB=7, PC=9. Put A=(0,0), B=(b,0), C=(0,c), and P=(x,y), with P inside the triangle. Complete the rectangle with fourth vertex H=(b,c). Then AH=sqrt(b^2+c^2)=BC. Compute PH^2=(b-x)^2+(c-y)^2. From the three given distances: PA^2=x^2+y^2=9, PB^2=(b-x)^2+y^2=49, PC^2=x^2+(c-y)^2=81, so PH^2=PB^2+PC^2-PA^2=49+81-9=121, hence PH=11. In triangle APH, AH <= AP+PH=3+11=14, so BC=AH <=14. Equality is attainable when A,P,H are collinear; for example choose H so AH=14 and P lies on AH with AP=3, giving a valid interior point configuration. Therefore the maximum BC is 14.

method.method_draft: Use the circumcenter of the right triangle. First read the image as a right triangle ABC with P inside and connected to all three vertices; BC is the hypotenuse because the text says angle BAC=90°. Let O be the midpoint of BC. Since ABC is right-angled at A, O is the circumcenter and OA=OB=OC=R, where BC=2R. Use vectors from O: let B=q, C=-q with |q|=R, let A=a with |a|=R, and let P=p. From the text, PB=7 and PC=9, so |p-q|^2+|p+q|^2=49+81=130, giving 2(|p|^2+R^2)=130 and hence |p|^2+R^2=65. Also PA=3 gives |p-a|^2=9, so |p|^2+R^2-2p·a=9; using the previous equation gives p·a=28. By Cauchy-Schwarz, p·a <= |p|R, so |p|R >=28. Let t=R^2. Since |p|^2=65-R^2, the inequality becomes t(65-t)>=784. Thus t^2-65t+784<=0, whose roots are 16 and 49, so R^2<=49 and R<=7. raw_record.original_question: Given the diagram, $P$ is a point inside the right-angled triangle $ABC$ where $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, and $PA=3$, $PB=7$, $PC=9$. What is the maximum value of $BC$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw PD$\perp$AB at D, PF$\perp$AC at F, then draw BG$\perp$PF at G through B, and CE$\perp$PD at E through C, intersecting BG at H, connect AH, PH\\
$\because$ $\angle$BAC$=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ the quadrilaterals ADPF, ADEC, ABGF, PGHE, and ABHC are all rectangles\\
$\therefore$ PD=BG, PF=AD=EC, PG=HE, BC=AH\\
$\therefore$ $PA^{2}=AD^{2}+PD^{2}=PF^{2}+PD^{2}$\\
$PC^{2}=EC^{2}+PE^{2}=PF^{2}+PE^{2}$\\
$PH^{2}=PE^{2}+HE^{2}=PE^{2}+PG^{2}$\\
$PB^{2}=PG^{2}+BG^{2}=PG^{2}+PD^{2}$\\
$\therefore$ $PB^{2}+PC^{2}=PA^{2}+PH^{2}=PF^{2}+PE^{2}+PG^{2}+PD^{2}$\\
$\because$PA=3, PB=7, PC=9\\
$\therefore$ $7^{2}+9^{2}=3^{2}+PH^{2}$,\\
Solving gives $PH=11$\\
$\because$ in $\triangle PAH$, PA=3, $PH=11$\\
$\therefore$ $8<AH<14$\\
$\because$ when points A, P, H are collinear, $AH=14$\\
$\therefore$ when points A, P, H are collinear, $BC=AH=14$ is the maximum\\
Hence, the answer is: $BC=\boxed{14}$
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, P is located inside the triangle, and PA, PB, PC are connected. The problem text gives angle BAC = 90°, and PA=3, PB=7, PC=9.

Reasoning: According to the coordinate/completing rectangle method, let A=(0,0), B=(b,0), C=(0,c), then BC=sqrt(b^2+c^2). Let P=(x,y), and complete the fourth vertex of the rectangle H=(b,c), then AH=sqrt(b^2+c^2)=BC, and PH^2=(b-x)^2+(c-y)^2.
From the known distances: PA^2=x^2+y^2=9, PB^2=(b-x)^2+y^2=49, PC^2=x^2+(c-y)^2=81. Thus PH^2=PB^2+PC^2-PA^2=49+81-9=121, so PH=11.
In triangle APH, AP=3, PH=11, therefore AH <= AP+PH=14. Also because AH=BC, so BC <=14.
When A, P, H are collinear and P is on segment AH, equality can be taken; at this time AH=AP+PH=14, and a situation in which P is located inside triangle ABC can be constructed, so the maximum value can be reached.
